# Feature Store Documentation — Tricura ML Case

**Output file:** `data/feature_store/feature_matrix_7d.parquet`  
**Generated by:** `exploration/02_feature_engineering.ipynb`  
**Observation unit:** resident × 7-day non-overlapping window  
**Total features:** 211 | **Total columns:** 218 (+ 5 meta + 2 targets)

---

## Temporal Design

```
◄── Feature lookback (varies by group) ──►│ 1d gap │◄── Label window ──►
                                          t-1d      t                 t+7d
```

- **Signal window:** Jul 2023 – Jan 2025 (bounded by vitals coverage)
- **Embargo:** features use data with timestamps ≤ `t − 1 day` to prevent leakage
- **Stride:** 7 days (non-overlapping); each resident-week is one independent row

---

## Observation Spine

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | String | Primary key — resident identifier |
| `facility_id` | String | Facility the resident belongs to |
| `window_start` | Datetime | `t` — start of the label window |
| `window_end` | Datetime | `t + 7d` — end of the label window |
| `feature_cutoff` | Datetime | `t − 1d` — last allowed timestamp for feature data |
| `split` | String | `train` / `test` / `holdout` (see Temporal Split) |

---

## Target Labels

| Column | Type | Positive rate | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fall_7d` | Int8 (0/1) | ~2.4% | Any `Fall` incident with `occurred_at ∈ [window_start, window_end)` |
| `rth_7d` | Int8 (0/1) | ~0.8% | Any **unplanned** hospital transfer with `effective_date ∈ [window_start, window_end)` |

**RTH definition:** `planned_flag = False OR planned_flag IS NULL` (97.5% of all transfers are unplanned).

---

## Temporal Split

| Split | Windows | Residents | fall_7d rate | rth_7d rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `train` | 38,389 | 1,749 | 2.25% | 0.72% |
| `test` | 24,311 | 1,712 | 2.62% | 0.95% |
| `holdout` | 3,612 | 1,007 | 2.91% | 0.80% |

- **Train:** `window_start < 2024-07-01`
- **Test:** `2024-07-01 ≤ window_start < 2025-01-01`
- **Hold-out:** `window_start ≥ 2025-01-01` (January 2025, simulates first production deployment)

## Feature Groups

### 1. Demographics
**Source:** `residents` | **Coverage:** ~100% | **Null handling:** fill 0 / computed

| Feature | Description | Null rate |
|---|---|---|
| `age_at_window` | Resident age in years at `window_start` (from `date_of_birth`) | ~0.1% |
| `los_days` | Length of stay in days at `window_start` (from `admission_date`) | 0.0% |

---

### 2. Vitals — Rolling Statistics
**Source:** `vitals` | **Coverage:** ~82% of residents | **Null handling:** null = no measurement in that window (LightGBM handles natively)

Vitals are clipped to physiologically valid ranges before aggregation to prevent data entry errors (e.g., BP = 13,385 mmHg) from corrupting rolling statistics:

| Vital type | Clipping range |
|---|---|
| BP - Systolic | [60, 250] mmHg |
| Pulse | [20, 200] bpm |
| O2 sats | [50, 100] % |
| Blood Sugar | [20, 600] mg/dL |
| Temperature | [90, 108] °F |
| Respiration | [5, 60] breaths/min |
| Pain Level | [0, 10] |
| Weight | [50, 500] lbs |

For each of the 8 vital types × 3 lookback windows (3d, 7d, 14d), 5 statistics are computed — **120 features total**.

**Naming convention:** `{vital_type}_{stat}_{lookback}` — e.g., `bp___systolic_mean_7d`

| Statistic suffix | Description |
|---|---|
| `_mean_{N}d` | Mean value over the last N days |
| `_std_{N}d` | Standard deviation over the last N days |
| `_min_{N}d` | Minimum value over the last N days |
| `_max_{N}d` | Maximum value over the last N days |
| `_count_{N}d` | Number of measurements in the last N days |

Typical null rates by vital type (3d / 7d / 14d lookback):

| Vital type | 3d null | 7d null | 14d null | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pain_level` | 48% | 46% | 45% | Most frequently measured |
| `bp___systolic` | 63% | 56% | 52% | Measured every 2–3 days |
| `pulse` | 64% | 57% | 52% | Co-measured with BP |
| `temperature` | 72% | 64% | 58% | |
| `o2_sats` | 73% | 66% | 61% | |
| `respiration` | 76% | 68% | 61% | |
| `blood_sugar` | 85% | 84% | 83% | Only routine for diabetic residents |
| `weight` | 87% | 76% | 62% | Measured weekly or less |

---

### 3. Vitals — Monitoring Flags
**Source:** `vitals` (derived) | **Coverage:** 100% (no nulls) | **Null handling:** explicit 0/1

Binary flags indicating whether a vital type was measured at least once in a given window. These make the absence of monitoring an explicit, unambiguous signal for the model — distinct from a null caused by missing data for other reasons.

**Naming convention:** `{vital_type}_measured_{lookback}` — e.g., `bp___systolic_measured_7d`

**24 features total** (8 vital types × 3 lookbacks). All have 0% null rate.

| Feature example | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pain_level_measured_3d = 1` | At least one pain level reading in the last 3 days |
| `weight_measured_7d = 0` | No weight recorded in the last 7 days |

---

## Tables Excluded from PoC

The following tables were excluded due to insufficient coverage relative to the vitals signal window (Jul 2023 – Jan 2025), which would produce too sparse features to be useful at the population level:

| Table | Resident coverage | Reason excluded |
|---|---|---|
| `medications` | 16% (35 facilities only) | Partial facility rollout; polypharmacy features would be missing for 84% of residents |
| `adl_responses` | 3.2% (9 facilities, Apr 2024–) | Too sparse; date range barely overlaps vitals window |
| `gg_responses` | 4.5% (18 facilities) | Too sparse for population-level features |
| `therapy_tracks` | 7.3% (15 facilities) | Insufficient coverage for reliable feature signal |

These tables may be re-introduced in later iterations as supplementary features with appropriate null handling (LightGBM native missing support).

---

## Notes on Null Values and Missing Data Strategy

- **Vitals stat columns** (`*_mean_*`, `*_std_*`, etc.): null means no measurements existed in that lookback window for that resident. LightGBM treats null as a separate split direction and learns its predictive value natively — no imputation needed.
- **Vitals measured flags** (`*_measured_*`): always 0 or 1, never null. Explicitly encode absence of monitoring as a feature.
- **Diagnosis flags** (24.2% null): null means the resident has no diagnosis records at all (vs. `0` which means records exist but none match the code). This distinction is meaningful and preserved.
- **History, needs, labs, tags** (0% null): filled with 0 when a resident has no matching records, since absence of prior events is a valid and informative value.
